clue.text: Coins perfect name I wanted for tiny creature

parts.note: silver is coinage, loose change

indicators.note: wanted in the sense of lacking, so the name and the I go missing from the word for perfect

parts.note: to perfect something is to finish it

explanation.surface: Someone frets that coins and a flawless name were missing, all for some tiny creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted' means lacking: N and I go missing from FINISH, leaving FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The silverfish is a small wingless insect found in damp corners of houses.

clue.text: Boggy place overlooking large reservoir

indicators.note: overlooking in the sense of ignoring or leaving out, so the large letter is dropped

parts.note: slump is a dialect word for a marshy, boggy patch of ground
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A marsh sits on high ground above a large water reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' looks like a position word in a down clue, but it means missing out: SLUMP without L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or well where liquid collects, a small reservoir, as in an engine's oil sump.

clue.text: Touring Northern Ireland county, learn about estate proprietor

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the shuffled letters go around the county
about signals that the letters of learn are moved around

parts.note: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone travelling around an Irish county is told to learn about a landed proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: A landowner is someone who owns land, such as the holder of a country estate.

clue.text: Heading off almost before appointed time

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: almost means nearly

explanation.surface: Someone sets off nearly ahead of the scheduled time.
explanation.walkthrough: NEARLY loses its head, the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving early means turning up ahead of the agreed hour.

clue.text: Voice bellowing out with obscure musical instrument

parts.note: to fog is to obscure or blur
a horn is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: A loud voice competes with a little-known musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' reads as an adjective for the instrument but is the verb, fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A foghorn voice is a loud, booming one, after the ship's warning siren.

clue.text: Footballer, one barely running, essentially having international replacement

indicators.note: essentially points to the heart of the word, its two central letters
replacement says those central letters are swapped for the international letter

parts.note: a streaker runs naked, barely dressed, across a pitch

explanation.surface: A footballer, a near-naked pitch invader and an international substitute all on one field.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters EA of STREAKER give way to I. A streaker is someone who runs naked across a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A striker is the forward whose job is to score goals.

clue.text: A graduate fired by incredible energy

indicators.note: fired as in sacked, so these letters are thrown out of the word for incredible

parts.note: incredible means amazing
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate fired up by some incredible energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests inspired, but it means dismissed: A and MA leave AMAZING.
explanation.definitionFit: Zing is lively vigour or zest, an informal word for energy.

clue.text: Extremely imposing facilities in domed residence up north?

indicators.note: the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: facilities is a polite word for a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: Remarkably impressive washrooms in a domed home in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: an Inuit snow house in the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped shelter of snow blocks built in Arctic regions.

clue.text: Resolved along with wife to keep posh poultry

indicators.note: to keep means the rearranged letters hold the posh letter inside
resolved in the sense of broken down and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Someone decides, with their wife, to keep some upmarket poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' looks like a verb meaning decided, but it is the signal to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Guineafowl are African game birds kept as farmyard poultry.

clue.text: City of Lincoln right to expect rising poverty

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, US president

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: need is poverty or want

explanation.surface: The city of Lincoln is right to expect poverty to increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City of Lincoln' looks like one phrase about the English city, but City is the definition and Lincoln is Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a major city on the north-east coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Fairly insignificant flier read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud says the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a flier is a bird, here the mynah

explanation.surface: A rather unimportant leaflet is read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a printed leaflet, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means lesser or of small importance.

clue.text: US soldier eating mostly dry, plain biscuit

indicators.note: eating means the soldier takes the other letters inside

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: arid means dry
bald means plain or blunt, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: An American soldier eats a dry, plain biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A garibaldi is a British biscuit with a squashed-currant filling.
explanation.definitionFit: The garibaldi is a thin currant-filled biscuit named after the Italian patriot.

clue.text: Flawless set of rules heralded by model

indicators.note: heralded by means preceded by, so the model comes first

parts.note: a copy is a model to be followed
the book is the rules, as in by the book

explanation.surface: A perfect rulebook introduced by a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' reads as a person, but it is a pattern to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Copybook as an adjective means exemplary, done exactly as taught in a handwriting primer.

clue.text: Greek character: individual sharing love for foreign flower

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: sharing means the O at the join is used once for both words

parts.note: one is a single individual
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Greek character and another person share a love of a foreign flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, a thing that flows; RHO and ONE overlap on their shared O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river flowing through Switzerland and France.

clue.text: Advise Bruce endlessly to train as frogman

indicators.note: train in the sense of shaping or directing, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the name is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone advises Bruce to train non-stop to become a frogman.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVISE plus BRUC (Bruce without its end) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A frogman is an underwater swimmer equipped with breathing apparatus, a scuba diver.

clue.text: Fitting some shelving I'd no choice over

indicators.note: over means the letters are turned round and read backwards
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A shelf unit was fitted because there was no other option.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading backwards through shelvING I'D NO Choice gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Condign means appropriate or deserved, used chiefly of punishment.

clue.text: Popular wine (Lombardy) drained with eagerness

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: drained means emptied of its inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A popular Lombardy wine is drunk keenly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a dark Spanish red wine; LOMBARDY drained leaves LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Intently means with close, eager concentration.

clue.text: Rapidly tell dance has been cancelled

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
off means cancelled, as in the match is off

explanation.surface: Someone quickly announces that the dance has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off a list is to recite it quickly and without effort.

clue.text: Attentive and obedient butler initially on retainer

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: a retainer is a servant in a household

explanation.surface: An attentive, obedient butler is kept on a retainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obedient' looks like a second definition, but only its initial is used; 'retainer' suggests a fee, but is an old servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice things, watchful.

clue.text: Considered discount food shop being carpeted

indicators.note: discount means disregard, so the shop is taken out

parts.note: deliberated means considered or weighed up
a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

explanation.surface: A cheap grocery is judged to be getting a new carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discount food shop' reads as a cut-price store, but discount is the verb, taking DELI from DELIBERATED. To carpet someone is British slang for to reprimand them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carpeted is being called in for a telling-off, which is being scolded.

clue.text: Contempt shown by dad is awkward at home

indicators.note: awkward means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Father shows scorn because he feels uncomfortable at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is scorn or a feeling that something is beneath one.

clue.text: Worker's adept at first with tool

parts.note: a hand is a worker, so worker's gives hand's

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of adept is used

explanation.surface: A worker is skilled from the start with a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is kept: HAND'S becomes HANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsaw is a saw worked by one hand, a carpenter's tool.

clue.text: Excellent cloth, it's said, for cleanliness

indicators.note: it's said signals a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: high is excellent or superior, and jean is a hard-wearing twilled cotton cloth

explanation.surface: A fine cloth is said to be good for keeping things clean.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH JEAN, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygiene is the practice of keeping clean to protect health.

clue.text: Skilful performer in protest against station's closure

indicators.note: against means beside or next to, so the closing letter is set next to the protest

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration, a protest

indicators.note: closure means the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A star performer joins a protest against shutting a station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demon' is a skilful expert, as in a demon bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon at something is an expert, a fiercely skilled performer.

clue.text: Aggressively virile current husband punches married Lothario finally

indicators.note: punches as in pierces, so these letters go into the others
finally means the last letter of the word

parts.note: AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A current husband thumps a married womaniser at last.
explanation.walkthrough: AC and H go inside M and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes an aggressive, showy kind of manliness.

clue.text: Chat about Italian's love for Native American chief

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gas is idle chat, talk
amore is the Italian word for love

explanation.surface: Someone chats about an Italian's affection for a tribal chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagamore is an Algonquian word for a chief of a Native American tribe.

clue.text: Tree pollen regularly shed behind old lady

indicators.note: behind means following, so the kept letters come after the mother

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, the old lady

indicators.note: regularly shed means every other letter is lost, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A tree sheds pollen at intervals behind an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: P, L, E are the first, third and fifth letters of POLLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a broad-leaved tree, source of maple syrup.

clue.text: Obligation to pay union

definitions.meaning: a certificate of debt, an obligation to repay
a tie or union between people

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a trade union's subscription; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a debt security issued by a borrower and a link or tie joining things.

clue.text: Making a comeback, Metallica vocalist holds sway

indicators.note: Making a comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
holds means the following words contain the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal band's singer returns and wields power.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'holds sway' as the definition, but vacillate means sway alone; 'holds' is the signal that the letters are contained in 'Metallica vocalist'.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver or swing between options, to sway back and forth.

clue.text: Joanna adding negative reply to sanctimonious article

definitions.note: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano

parts.note: pi is short for pious, sanctimonious
a is the indefinite article
no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: Joanna adds a refusal to a holier-than-thou piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joanna' looks like a woman's name but is Cockney rhyming slang (Joanna rhymes with piano in a Cockney accent).
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a joanna is the musical instrument with keys and hammers.

clue.text: Good to move out of train compartment

indicators.note: move out of means leave, so the good letter is removed

parts.note: to groom someone is to train them

explanation.surface: It is good to leave a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train compartment' reads as a railway carriage; train is the verb, groom.
explanation.definitionFit: A room is an enclosed division of a building, a compartment.

clue.text: Achievement Dundee surprisingly claims, not losing any games

indicators.note: claims means takes in, so the shuffled letters surround the achievement
surprisingly means the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: a feat is an achievement

explanation.surface: Dundee, a football team, unexpectedly claims a record of no defeats.
explanation.definitionFit: Undefeated means unbeaten, never having lost a match.
